scope: One pinned upstream repository feature, three matched repeats per entrant. Diagnostic evidence; no universal or statistically established product ranking.
budget_basis: Reuse the existing task bench default of 600 seconds per step. Three repeats follow its documented diagnostic recommendation; they do not establish statistical superiority.
intervention_policy: No code corrections, hidden-check feedback, retries, or model switches within an attempt. Preserve all planned cells including errors, timeouts and unstarted cells. A harness defect stops or invalidates affected evidence before a new campaign, rather than changing the task during execution.
success: The provider completes successfully; every frozen test passes with complete identity receipts and no skips; relevant tests and documentation are added; review confirms the diff satisfies the provided contract without collateral regressions.
configuration: Identical upstream checkout and task prompt; Codex native workspace-write sandbox, no command network, ignored user config/rules, private HOME/CODEX_HOME. Bruhs retains its normal system contract and tools backed by isolated synthetic stores. Native CLI shared daemon, automatic skill instructions/bundled skills, remote plugins, native app connectors and memories are explicitly disabled in both paths; Bruhs own application MCP tools remain available.
limits: One feature and one public upstream repository; model familiarity or training overlap is unknown.
Only selected standard-library regressions run; unavailable optional-backend matrices and one absolute-host-path FileLock case are excluded before model access.
Provider sandbox permits some host reads. Hidden checks/reference are withheld from workspace and prompt but this is not an adversarial secrecy evaluation.
Token volume is not money; billed cost and complete human/machine cost remain unknown.
No Capy, Claude Code, T3 Code, product-default campaign or complete personal-workflow delivery is included.
aggregation: All six planned cells remain in the denominator. Failure, timeout, harness error and unstarted are distinct outcomes; none may be dropped or counted as success. Manual diff-review failures override automatic test success.
controlled_factors: upstream source commit and starting records
task prompt and public smoke checks
fresh provider sessions and private application stores
intentional_product_differences: Bruhs normal system instructions, response contract and available app tools
direct installed Codex CLI versus Bruhs API/SDK transport
runtime_verification: Each settled provider rollout must contain no automatic skills catalog. Retain initial-message fingerprints; stop and retain all planned cells if actual runtime context fails this policy.
revision_note: Version 2 follows retained campaign-01, stopped after discovering uncontrolled four-versus-58 skill catalogs. The original task prompt is unchanged. Three finite-integer review probes are now part of the predeclared frozen feature checks.
model_configuration_basis: Reuse GPT-6.1 Sol at low effort from the earlier live pilot so repository coverage changes without also changing model/effort. This controlled configuration is separate from a product-default campaign.
